Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 1:

﴿ʿAmma﴾ (about what?) ﴿yatasa'alun﴾ (they ask one another). Some of the Quraysh ask one another.
﴿About the great news﴾ explains "that thing." The interrogative form is used to magnify it. It is what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought of the Qur'an, which includes the resurrection and other matters.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 3:

﴿Concerning which they dispute﴾, so the believers affirm it and the disbelievers deny it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn, commentary on Surah an-Naba' (78), verse 4:

﴿Nay, indeed!﴾ (a rebuke) ﴿They will come to know﴾ what will befall them because of their denial of it.

﴿Then no! They will come to know.﴾ "Kalla" (no/nay) is an emphasis (ta'kid) and is repeated here for reinforcement. The particle "thumma" (then) is used here to indicate that the second threat is more severe than the first. Then He, exalted is He, pointed to the power to resurrect, saying: "Did We not make the earth a resting-place?"
﴿Have We not made the earth a resting-place?﴾ A bed (firash) like a cradle (mahd).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 7:

﴿And the mountains as pegs﴾ by which the earth is kept firm, just as tents are kept firm by pegs. The interrogative (istifham) here is for affirmation (taqrir).

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 8:**

﴿And We created you in pairs﴾ males and females.
﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾, a repose for your bodies.
﴿And We made the night a garment﴾, covering with its darkness.
﴿And We made the day a time for livelihood﴾, a time for seeking one's means of living.
﴿And We built above you seven﴾ seven heavens, ﴿strong﴾, the plural of شَدِيدَة (shadīdah), meaning firm and well-made, such that the passing of time has no effect on them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 13:

﴿And We made a lamp﴾ bright, ﴿blazing﴾ burning intensely: meaning the sun.

﴿And We send down from the rain-laden clouds⟩ (al-mu'sirat), the clouds that are due to pour rain, like the girl (mu'sir) who has come near to menstruation. ﴿Water pouring forth abundantly⟩, meaning, pouring down in torrents.
﴿That We may bring forth thereby grain﴾ like wheat, ﴿and vegetation﴾ like figs.
﴿And gardens﴾, orchards, ﴿intertwined﴾, densely entangled; it is the plural of lafif, like sharif and ashraf.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision﴾ between the creatures ﴿was an appointed time﴾, a time for reward and punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 18:

﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in multitudes﴾ "The Trumpet" (al-Ṣūr) is the horn; it is in apposition to "the Day of Decision" (yawm al-faṣl), or is an explanation of it. The one who blows it is Isrāfīl (Israfil). ﴿And you will come﴾ from your graves to the place of standing (al-mawqif). ﴿In multitudes﴾ (afwājan): groups, of various kinds.
﴿And the sky will be opened﴾, with both the intensive (tashdid) and the light (takhfif) readings, split apart for the descent of the angels, ﴿so it will become gateways﴾, having gates.
ﷻ "And the mountains will be set in motion" — they will be taken away from their places. "So they will become a mirage" — dust, i.e., like it in the lightness of its movement.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 78, verse 21:

﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever waiting in ambush﴾ — ready to receive them, or prepared (for the transgressors).
For the tyrants (al-taghin), the disbelievers, so they will not pass beyond it, a place of return (ma'aban) for them, so they will enter it.

The translation of this passage, from the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 23:

﴿Lābithīna﴾ (remaining) is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl muqaddara), meaning: their staying is predetermined. ﴿Fīhā aḥqābān﴾ (therein for ages): ages (duhūr) without any end. It is the plural of ḥuqb (ḥuqb), with its first letter vocalized with a ḍamma.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 24:

﴿They shall not taste therein any coolness﴾ — sleep; for they shall not taste it. ﴿Nor any drink﴾ — that which is drunk for pleasure.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 25:

﴿Except﴾ rather, ﴿hameem﴾ water that is hot, extremely hot, ﴿and ghassaq﴾ (pronounced with both the light and the heavy forms): the discharge that flows from the pus of the people of the Fire. ﴿They will taste it﴾, ﴿recompensed﴾ with that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 26:

﴿A fitting recompense﴾ corresponding to their deeds. For there is no sin greater than disbelief, and no punishment greater than the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 27:

﴿Indeed, they used not to expect﴾ (yakhāfūna), i.e., fear, ﴿a reckoning﴾, because of their denial of the resurrection (al-ba'th).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 28:

﴿And they denied Our signs﴾ the Qur'an ﴿with complete denial﴾ (kidhdhaban), meaning, a denial (takdhiban).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 29:

﴿And everything﴾ of the deeds ﴿We have enumerated﴾, We have kept account of it, ﴿in a Book﴾ by writing it down in the Preserved Tablet, ﴿so that We may recompense for it﴾, and among that is their denial of the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 30:

﴿So taste⦆ meaning: it will be said to them in the Hereafter, when the punishment befalls them, "Taste your recompense." ﴿So We shall not increase you except in punishment﴾ over your punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 31:

﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing is an achievement (mafaz)﴾ — a place of triumph (fawz) in Paradise.

Gardens: enclosed orchards, in apposition to "fawza" (a place of triumph), or an explanation of it. "And grapevines": coordinated with "mafazan" (a place of triumph).

Note on the glosses: the passage is a grammatical comment, so the Arabic terms it discusses are kept in Arabic script above, with the English explanation alongside.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 78, verse 33:

﴿And maidens with swelling breasts⦆ — جَوارِي (jawari, young women) whose breasts have become firm and rounded (تَكَعَّبَتْ ثُدِيّهنَّ), plural of كاعِب (kti'ib, a maiden with firm, rounded breasts). ﴿of equal age﴾ — عَلى سِنّ واحِد (of one single age), plural of تِرْب (tirb, a companion of the same age), pronounced with a kasra on the taa' and a sukun on the raa'.
﴿And a cup overflowing﴾: wine filling its vessels. In Surat al-Qital (the chapter of Muhammad, 47), it says: "and rivers of wine."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 35:

﴿They will not hear therein﴾ i.e., in Paradise, during the drinking of wine or other circumstances, ﴿any vain speech﴾ (laghw), falsehood of speech, ﴿nor any lying﴾ (kidhdhaban). With the light pronunciation (takhfif) it means falsehood (kadhiban); with the heavy pronunciation (tashdid), it means denial (takdhiban), by one person to another, unlike what occurs in this world during the drinking of wine.

﴿A recompense from your Lord﴾, meaning God rewarded them with a recompense, ﴿a gift﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "recompense," ﴿in abundance﴾, meaning plentiful, from their saying: أعْطانِي فَأَحْسَبنِي (a'taanee fa-ahsabanee), meaning he gave me so much that he made me say "enough" (hasbee).

Lord of the heavens and the earth, [read] in the genitive (rabbi) and the nominative (rabbu); and what is between them, the Most Merciful (al-Rahman). [Read] likewise, and with the nominative of "al-Rahman" alongside the genitive of "rabb." They do not possess (la yamlikun), i.e., the creatures, from Him, exalted is He, any address (khitab), i.e., no one is able to address Him out of fear of Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 38:

﴿Yawm﴾ (the Day) is an adverbial complement (zarf) for "they will not have power" (lā yamlikūn) ﴿yaqūm al-rūḥ﴾ (when the Spirit stands), i.e., Jibril, or the soldiers of Allah ﴿wa-l-malā'ika ṣaffan﴾ (and the angels in rows) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning arranged in ranks ﴿lā yatakallamūn﴾ (they will not speak), i.e., the creatures ﴿illā man adhina lahu al-Raḥmān﴾ (except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted) to speak ﴿wa-qāla﴾ (and he says) a word ﴿ṣawāban﴾ (correct) from among the believers and the angels, such as interceding for those whom He is pleased with.

That day is the true (certain) day, whose occurrence is established, and it is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So whoever wills, let him take to his Lord a return (maʼab)﴾, i.e., a place of return, meaning he returns to Allah through His obedience, so that he may be safe from the punishment on that day.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 78, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, We have warned you﴾ O disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿of a near punishment﴾, the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, which is coming, and everything that is coming is near. ﴿The Day﴾ is an adverbial complement (ẓarf) relating to ʿadhāban (punishment) by its description, ﴿when a man will look at what his hands have sent forward﴾, every individual, of good and evil, ﴿and the disbeliever will say: "Oh (yā, an interjection of exclamation)! ﴾, ﴿Would that I were dust!"﴾ meaning, so that I would not be punished. He says this when, after the retribution is carried out among the animals, Allah the Exalted says to them: "Be dust!"
